facts.text: The ACTIONS list defines five actions, in order (-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (0, -1) and (0, 0)
The action space is Discrete(nA), where nA is the length of the ACTIONS list
GoalGridworld-v0 is registered with entry point multiworld.envs.gridworlds.goal_gridworld:GoalGridworld and no keyword arguments
The constructor's default grid is 10 rows by 10 columns
The observation space is a Dict with the members observation, achieved_goal and desired_goal; each member is a Box of shape (rows, columns, 1) with low 0 and high 1
A reset draws the agent cell and the goal cell from one random permutation of all grid cells, so the two cells are distinct, and starts the step count at 0
move_agent adds the action's offset to the agent row and column and keeps the old cell when the move would leave the grid
An episode ends after 41 steps: the step count is incremented and done becomes true when the count is greater than 40
The reward is the negative sum of squared differences between the achieved and desired flattened observations
The achieved observation image is 1 at the agent cell and 0.2 at each in-bounds diagonal neighbour
The desired observation image is 0.2 at every in-bounds cell of the goal's 3 x 3 neighbourhood and 1 at the goal cell itself
The step info carries success 0, the step count and the done flag

determinism.notes: the fake backend seeds Python's random.Random from reset(seed); one seed and one action sequence repeat the state hashes.  Upstream reset() takes no seed and draws from the global numpy generator (goal_gridworld.py:71), so this seed control is a property of the fake, not of the upstream class

gaps: event-driven analytic grid model: one tick is one move on a 10 x 10 grid, so timestep_ms is 0 and there are no dynamics, forces, contacts, actuator, sensor or noise models
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, only step commands advance the episode

the fake re-implements the upstream class in pure Python and was not compared with the upstream environment; it uses Python's random.Random for the reset, upstream uses the unseeded global numpy generator
no rendering: the upstream render() method needs OpenCV and writes a PNG outside the package, so the fake omits render and the observation grid is the only visual output

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the grid state is kept and stays readable
